Text 1
Film scholars have struggled with the vastness of Japanese director Akira Kurosawa's collective body of work (spanning over 30 films in total). It is best, however, to understand Kurosawa's filmography thematically. Kurosawa's cinematic output can be considered to fall into three major thematic categories, with each one representing a particular narrative and visual cohesion: samurai epics, contemporary social dramas, and adaptations of literary works.

Text 2
It is tempting to impose thematic order on the expanse of Akira Kurosawa's body of work as a filmmaker. However, critics who have considered Kurosawa's films to fit neatly into distinct thematic categories overlook potential stylistic elements in Kurosawa's work that span across these categories. Additionally, this view may discount significant differences in the approach and content of films grouped within the same thematic category.
prompt: Which choice best describes a difference in how the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 view the study of Kurosawa's films?

choices.A: Although the author of Text 1 claims that Kurosawa's filmmaking approach has varied by theme, the author of Text 2 argues that Kurosawa's style has remained uniform across all his works.
choices.B: While the author of Text 1 believes that thinking about Kurosawa's films in thematic categories is useful, the author of Text 2 views such an approach as limiting.
choices.C: The author of Text 1 considers Kurosawa's films to showcase his strongest artistic achievements, whereas the author of Text 2 believes that Kurosawa's photography is where he is most skilled.
choices.D: The author of Text 1 argues that Kurosawa's samurai films were his most technically innovative, whereas the author of Text 2 claims that Kurosawa's social dramas demonstrate greater technical mastery.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The author of Text 1 states that Kurosawa's cinematic output can be considered to fall into three major thematic categories, implying that this is a helpful way to understand his films. The author of Text 2, on the other hand, challenges this view and says that it overlooks potential stylistic elements and differences in Kurosawa's work across what Text 1 calls distinct thematic categories.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. Neither text discusses the technical innovation of Kurosawa's films, nor do they make any claims about which category demonstrates greater technical mastery.
